newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-French poll worries hit Paris stocks, dollar.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-French poll worries hit Paris stocks, dollar.

text.p: Speculation over a snap French election pulled down Paris stocks on Monday and weakened the dollar as currency investors turned to the mark.
The U.S. currency slipped nearly a pfennig as the French political uncertainty dented recent optimism over prospects for Europe's single currency and thus bolstered the mark.
London and Frankfurt also put on a lacklustre performance but Paris had the worst day, with the CAC-40 index dropping 1.24 percent before recovering slightly.

Investors expect President Jacques Chirac to call parliamentary elections on Monday evening as the government seeks a mandate to push through austerity measures aimed at qualifying France for a single European currency by 1999.
The franc hit its highest level against the mark since June 1993 at 3.3615 last Wednesday but slipped to 3.3725 on Monday as talk about the election grew.
Analysts said a win for the centre-right coalition, even with a sharply reduced majority, would cause French markets to rebound to the levels reached early last week.

But a Socialist victory could weaken the franc further and cause a sharp rise in short-term interest rates until a new government managed to convince markets that it would do what was necessary to meet the single currency criteria, they said.
In Frankfurt, floor trade was down 0.27 percent as the dollar's slide against the mark dimmed prospects for the exports sector before it clawed back the losses to edge into the plus column.
But the computerised IBIS index, down 0.83 precent at one stage, was still 0.38 percent down in late morning trading.
Daimler led trading volumes and suffered the second biggest losses in pre-bourse trade to decline 2.90 marks, or more than two percent, to 127.50 marks.
Its fall followed a report in Germany's mass circulation Bild newspaper which said the government planned a sharp increase in petrol tax before the summer.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, slipped in and out of profit in the morning session with worries over interest rates and the outcome of the May 1 election offset by the debut of Britain's newest bank, which surpassed expectations.
Shares in newly-floated Alliance & Leicester began trading at 542.5p before climbing as high as 556p in rapid early trade.
Other stocks were flat. "If it wasn't for A&L things would be very dull," one dealer commented.
"With the election coming up no-one really wants to commit themselves," a trader said. "That is why we did very little last week whilst Wall Street was roaring away."
On the currency front the dollar was hit by the stronger mark, losing a pfennig in early transactions.
"The French election speculation has given the mark overall strength," said a Japanese bank dealer.

Analysts said the new bout of jitters over prospects for Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) was because of worries that new government may be less willing to push through austerity measures to meet EMU criteria.
The dollar was also down half a yen and analysts said caution before next weekend's meeting of the G7 industrialised nations in Washington was likely to keep it subdued in the short term.

"The issue of the strong dollar (against the yen) is being linked into the G7 and the risk is for a strongly worded statement. This is keeping things steady and stable for the moment," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank in London.
The G7 meeting on April 27 is after a meeting between Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and U.S. President Bill Clinton on Friday, April 25.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7055 marks and 125.40 yen after ending at 1.7129 and 125.94 in late trading in Europe on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 2.0 points at 4,308.5
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 22.34 points at 2,525.22.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 3.19 points at 3,347.58.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $342.15 an ounce versus $342.45 at the close in London on Friday. Silver was two cents higher at $4.75.
